newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHESTERFIELD AND WREXHAM ENJOY THEIR MOMENT OF GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHESTERFIELD AND WREXHAM ENJOY THEIR MOMENT OF GLORY.

text.p: Chesterfield Football Club have not enjoyed a great deal of glory since they started playing football in 1866 -- but their long wait for a place in the spotlight is over.

On Monday their name made the headlines on both the front and back pages of newspapers all over Britain after they knocked premier league Nottingham Forest out of the F.A. Cup to reach the quarter-finals for the first time in their history -- which actually began five years before the Cup itself got going in the 1871-72 season.

Sunday's draw for the last eight then pitted them against Wrexham, also of the second division, which means that for the first time since 1984 and for only the seventh time ever, a team from outside the top two divisions in England will reach the semifinals.
Shock results have brought much of the old magic and romance back to the world's oldest knock-out cup competition this season.
None of the Big Five -- Manchester United, Liverpool, Everton, Tottenham and Arsenal -- are even left in the competition and for the first time since 1975 no Big Five team will be in the final.

For the first time since 1954 two teams from the third tier of English soccer have reached the last eight and the cup is now the most open since 1931 when only three teams from the top flight survived this far.
Five premier league clubs will compete in the last eight -- but only two are assured of a place in the last four.

Chesterfield have an immediate score to settle with Wrexham as the Welsh side beat them in the more familiar surroundings of the second round last season, and after beating Forest 1-0 on Saturday, Chesterfield must fancy their chances. Then again, after beating first division Birmingham 3-1 on Saturday, Wrexham fancy theirs.

"Saturday was one of the greatest days, if not the greatest day in the history of the club and so important for the players and the people of Chesterfield," said the club's owner J.Norton Lea, a former Forest fan.
"We haven't made a financial killing yet but in terms of prestige and kudos for the town its immeasurable."

Wrexham will become the first Welsh club since Swansea in 1964 to reach the semifinals if they beat Chesterfield, and the way they came back from a goal deficit to beat Birmingham should mean they have nothing to worry about.
"We came to Birmingham believing we had a chance and were capable of winning. We proved it, the dream continues," Wrexham manager Brian Flynn said afterwards.
And it still could, all the way to the last four -- if there were any logic in this season's competition, which clearly there is not.
After coming from behind to beat Newcastle United in the fourth round, not many people expected Forest to lose to Chestefield.
After winning 1-0 at Arsenal in the fourth round and going five matches without conceding a goal, not many people gave first division Portsmouth much of a chance at Leeds, where they triumphed 3-2.
Just about the only results which did go to form were Wimbledon's 2-1 win over Queens Park Rangers and Sheffield Wednesday's 1-0 win at Bradford City.
As it happens, they were both drawn together in the last eight. Only a very rich punter should risk his money on gambling on what is going to happen next.
